digest.component_or_area: review-bot LLM provider configuration and production cutover
propositions: The review bot must be cut over from direct Anthropic API to Bedrock inference profiles to validate that the dogfood path (Bedrock) matches the path rebar users take, surfacing provider-specific failures before clients encounter them.

The per-pass model split (frontier/standard/trivial classes) established in code-review.yaml and plan-review.yaml must be preserved post-cutover: Pass-1 on opus-family profiles, Pass-2/Pass-4 on sonnet-family profiles, with independent class-slot environment variables rather than a single scalar knob.

The cutover must include no cross-provider fallback; a degraded Bedrock must stop the gate cleanly rather than silently masking failures behind direct Anthropic, and the kill switch must restore the Anthropic path via class-slot deletion with a retained credential.

The review-bot container image must install pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock] extra so the provider module is present at runtime; boto3 presence alone is insufficient and produces false-negative health checks that mask import failures.

Production observability for Bedrock provider failures must exist before cutover: a native AWS/Bedrock metric-math alarm on InvocationClientErrors / Invocations dimensioned by ModelId, distinct from the VOTER_ERROR alarm, and the kill-switch runbook entry documenting the botocore retry/timeout posture (stock defaults, no rebar-configured retry envelope on the Bedrock path).

End-to-end verification must prove the cutover produces real votes on Bedrock inference profiles with nonzero prompt-cache reads, the per-pass model split resolves correctly in production usage logs, and the kill switch restores Anthropic-path voting with a working credential.
